items.title: 54270_Doc Cheatham oral history interview
items.q: it was three trumpets, Bobby Hackett, Clark Terry, and myself... I played with, as I said, Clark Terry, I worked with him, played with him

ctx.x: We had Nat Pierce, drummer, I never remember his name. The had a trio that Benny Morton and myself played -- the same trio played with Clark Terry and Bobby Brookmeyer. And then Maynard Ferguson's big band was on the program. And Benny Morton and myself sat in with Maynard's big band. Just for kicks, we didn't get paid for it but we I guess it saved Maynard a couple of salaries. But we did it, we volunteered to do it. His -- you know, he agreed, that he was happy to have us, so we played with his big band and…
We were in the big band, so we didn't get out there and get in the jam session at all. But it was a very nice tour, and a tour up and down the coast and back.

items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [inaudible comments from Terry on Jimmy Rushing, Joe Turner, Joe Williams, Doc Cheatham]

ctx.x: No, the reason he did that – he wanted people to know that we were two outstanding [inaudible]. They took it the opposite way. [Inaudible story about Barnet and Basie at the Royal Roost, including Ed Shaughnessy on drums, Bennie Green on trombone.] We also worked together on the bill with Basie’s small group and Charlie’s small group. It might have been during that period when I was possibly subbing for somebody, maybe Conte Candoli. [Inaudible reference to something involving Tommy Dorsey’s band with Charlie…

[inaudible comments from Terry on Jimmy Rushing, Joe Turner, Joe Williams, Doc Cheatham] [intermittently audible phrases reveal Terry telling stories that Brower asks him to repeat the following week (see below): on the formation of Basie’s small group; on his bringing Ernie Wilkins into Basie’s big band; on his joining Ellington; on Basie’s sense of tempo; on Ellington’s practice of writing for particular individuals, and Ellington’s composition Juniflip on the Flugelhorn, written for Terry; on Ellington…
